results.name: Required sections present
results.criterion: The lesson has an H2 section for each of: the prerequisite idea, what the topic is, why it matters, how it works, a worked example, limits, recap, a self-check quiz, and key words.

h2_headings: before we start: large language model

results.name: Short sentences
results.criterion: Average sentence length <= 15 words AND no sentence longer than 25 words.
evidence: (36 words) Finally, the LLM reads chunk twelve and generates the final answer: "The fine for returning a library book late is ten rupees per day." The answer is accurate because the model read the real rulebook page.
results.fix: Split every sentence longer than 25 words into two or three short sentences. One idea per sentence.

results.name: Plain-English readability
results.criterion: Flesch Reading Ease >= 60 on the lesson prose.

results.name: Right length for one sitting
results.criterion: Between 850 and 1800 words (~10-15 minutes of reading for a slow reader).

results.name: Self-check with answers
results.criterion: The quiz section has at least 3 questions and gives the answers.

results.name: Verified links to learn more
results.criterion: A 'Learn more' section links 2-4 resources, at least one a video, and EVERY link in the lesson is on the list verified live during research (no invented or broken URLs).

results.name: No false or misleading claims
results.criterion: Every technical claim agrees with the reference facts. No listed misconception is stated or implied as true. Simplifications are allowed only if they do not create a wrong belief (a misconception from the reference sheet, even softened, is a FAIL).
results.reasoning: Every item was verified against the reference facts and misconceptions list. All technical claims, definitions, and limits in the lesson match the reference accurately without introducing any prohibited misconceptions or false claims. I have verified all listed items against the lesson text and found every single quote present and completely accurate according to the reference facts. No misconceptions or technical inaccuracies are present in the rest of the text.

results.name: All must-cover points taught
results.criterion: Every must-cover point in the reference is actually taught (explained, not just named).
results.reasoning: Every required must-cover point from M1 through M9 was explicitly located in the text and verified against the reference specifications. The explanations provided in the lesson are clear, concise, and match all pedagogical guidelines.

results.name: Every technical term explained
results.criterion: Every technical or English-uncommon term is explained in simple words at or before its first use in the body (a glossary at the end alone does not count). Acronyms are expanded on first use.
results.reasoning: I checked every technical and uncommon term in the lesson against the requirement that it be explained in simple words at or before its first use. All terms such as large language model, LLM, prompt, retrieval, embedding, chunk, hallucination, and weights are properly defined or contextualized upon introduction.

results.name: Concrete analogy and walk-through
results.criterion: The lesson has (a) at least one everyday analogy a young Indian learner would recognise, correctly mapped to the topic, AND (b) one concrete worked example that follows a single case through every step the lesson lists under 'How does it work?', in order, to its result.
evidence: The worked example goes through EVERY step listed in the 'How does it work?' section, in the same order, applied to that one case (name any step it skips). -> "First, the college collects the rulebook PDF. The system splits the PDF into small chunks. It turns every chunk into a list of numbers representing meaning and stores them. This setup happens before any student asks a question. Next, a student types a question... It finds chunk number twelve... Then, the system copies chunk twelve into a prompt... Finally, the LLM reads chunk twelve and generates the final answer"
results.fix: In the 'Let's follow one example' section, explicitly label or write out sentences corresponding to storage and querying as numbers/embeddings so that every single one of the 7 steps from 'How does it work?' is tracked sequentially for the student's question.
results.reasoning: I checked the lesson for an everyday analogy and a complete worked example. The lesson includes a good analogy of a kirana shop owner and a college helpdesk bot example. However, item 4 fails because the 'How does it work?' section lists 7 distinct steps (Indexing, Embedding, Storage, Querying, Retrieval, Augmentation, Generation), whereas the worked example skips explicit mention of Step 3 (Storage) and Step 4 (Querying turning the question into an embedding) in sequence, blurring the step-by-step alignment.

results.name: Fits a non-native English beginner
results.criterion: Uses common, everyday English words; no idioms, slang, sarcasm or culturally obscure references; assumes no coding, maths beyond class 12, or prior AI knowledge; tone is encouraging and direct.
results.reasoning: I checked the lesson for idioms, uncommon vocabulary, assumed advanced knowledge, grammar errors, and tone. The English is simple and direct, uses everyday phrasing, explains all AI terms from scratch, contains no grammar mistakes, and appropriately addresses the learner as 'you'.

results.name: Builds step by step
results.criterion: Ideas are introduced before they are used; sections go from what -> why -> how -> example -> limits -> recap; each section links to the previous one; nothing is repeated without purpose.
results.reasoning: I checked the lesson flow against all requested requirements. Sections follow the exact planned order, terms are introduced before use, transitions between sections are smooth, analogies are appropriately placed, and references to retrieval build progressively from definition to step-by-step action, example application, and recap summary.

change_log.change: Targeted edits failed twice, so the lesson was rewritten from scratch with this failure given as an explicit constraint.
